source_quote: Glucosamine-based nutraceuticals showed variable efficacy in canine osteoarthritis, with stronger benefit in combination protocols.
EPA and DHA omega-3 supplementation reduced inflammatory mediators and improved pain scores in canine osteoarthritis.
Sulfur-based joint support compounds contributed to improved comfort scores in chronic canine spinal pain cohorts.
Chondroprotective substrates were associated with improved mobility outcomes in chronic degenerative spinal conditions.
Omega-3 fatty acid supplementation correlated with reduced airway inflammatory burden in upper respiratory canine conditions.
Omega-3 enriched diets reduced pruritus severity and inflammatory marker levels in atopic canine dermatology patients.
Trace zinc support improved epidermal barrier repair outcomes in canine inflammatory skin disease cohorts.
Natural oral biofilm-active compounds reduced plaque accumulation indices in daily canine dental care protocols.
Taurine supplementation was associated with improved cardiac functional markers in taurine-deficient canine cardiomyopathy.
Multi-strain probiotic administration reduced chronic stool instability frequency and supported gut barrier integrity in dogs.
L-carnitine supplementation improved lean mass retention and fat metabolism during canine weight reduction programs.
Antioxidant carotenoid supplementation including lutein slowed oxidative stress progression in canine senile cataract patients.
